sections.html:
Orem is a Utah County city roughly 45 miles down the interstate from Salt Lake City, close to where Utah Lake meets the valley's east shore. It spans 18.57 square miles at roughly 4,767 feet, with Provo to the east and south, Vineyard to the west and Lindon to the north.

Two roads organize the map. Interstate 15 runs down the west side with four interchanges inside the city, and US 89 (State Street) cuts through the middle from northwest to southeast. Cross streets including 800 North (Canyon Parkway), 1600 North, University Parkway and Geneva Road carry state route numbers. Shoppers tend to measure a house by its distance to State Street, University Parkway and the freeway, so know those numbers before you list.

Early farmers spread their homes along the old territorial highway, now State Street, and that pattern still shows. Older lots near State Street and the original grid differ a lot from the newer tracts built later.

The 2020 census put Orem at 98,129 people, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 95,214. Only Utah's four biggest cities are larger, and owners occupy a bit over half of the homes.

Treat these as city averages. Your own condition, lot and street can push a sale well above or below them.

The mix runs from detached houses to townhomes to apartment buildings, and the city posts the breakdown. Of 29,593 occupied units in the 2021 American Community Survey, 17,913 (60.5%) were owner-occupied and 11,680 (39.5%) were rented.

  • Single-family homes: 16,509 units, or 55.8% of occupied housing
  • Twinhomes and townhomes: 3,227 units, or 10.9%
  • Buildings with 10 or more apartments or condos: 4,434 units, or 15.0%
  • Mobile homes and other types: 575 units, or 1.9%

Selling a long-time rental is a different job from selling a home you lived in, since tenants, leases and put-off repairs all affect the timeline. Utah Valley University keeps renter demand strong around campus.

Orem permits an accessory apartment within a house, with one condition: the owner occupies either the main residence or the apartment. The city counted 752 legal accessory apartments as of June 2023, with 30 added in 2022 and 23 more in the first half of 2023.

That condition comes up at sale time. An apartment that was never registered, or one a past owner rented out from somewhere else, invites questions during a buyer's inspection. Detached accessory units are a newer topic under state law S.B. 284. Orem's proposed response would keep them out of front yards and bar short-term rental use, and the law reaches lots of 11,000 square feet or more. Before telling a buyer a detached unit is possible, find out from city planners where the rules stand.

FrontRunner has a station west of I-15, and a pedestrian bridge connects it to the UVU campus. UVX, a bus rapid transit line run jointly with Provo, connects Orem Central Station, UVU and University Parkway toward Provo. Average commute time for Orem workers is 20.1 minutes.

If your house is a short walk from the station or a UVX stop, say so in the listing.

Today Alpine School District covers Orem. On July 1, 2027 it is dissolved, and Orem goes to the new Timpanogos district with Pleasant Grove, Lindon and Vineyard. Voters approved the split in the 2024 general election, board members were elected in 2025 and superintendents were hired in 2026.

Parents will ask which district a house belongs to, and the answer is changing. Look up your exact address on the boundary map before you quote one.

The county sends each Orem owner a Notice of Property Valuation and Tax Changes near the end of July. To dispute the market value, file with the county Board of Equalization by September 15. The actual tax bill arrives between the middle and end of October.

A primary home earns a 45% residential exemption, which means the tax is figured on 55% of market value. To qualify, someone has to live there for at least 183 consecutive days a year: the owner, a relative or a full-time tenant. A rental without a full-time eligible occupant is treated as secondary and taxed on the full amount.

For payoff questions, call the Utah County Treasurer at 801-851-8255. Deeds are recorded by the county Recorder, 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300 in Provo, which will not draft paperwork, advise you legally or search titles. After a sale, the new owner may get a declaration form, and your closing agent can walk through it.

About 240 miles long, the Wasatch Fault has ten segments and five of them are active, including the Provo segment. That segment last produced a large quake roughly 200 to 700 years ago, and about 80% of Utah residents live along the fault.

Inspectors may note chimney bracing, water heater straps and foundation ties, and older brick homes get the most scrutiny. Selling as-is means none of it lands on your repair list.

sections.h2: What to have ready before you sell
sections.html: Pull together your deed or closing statement, the most recent valuation notice and tax bill, and any lease if the house is rented. If there is a basement apartment, look for whatever paperwork the city gave you when it was set up. Missing papers are common and usually fixable through the title company, but a short list of what you do have makes the first conversation easier and lets you ask better questions about timing, payoff and closing costs.

sections.h2: Selling an Orem house for cash
sections.html:
Owners reach out to us about an inherited house, a worn-out rental, a basement apartment with no paperwork, or a move with a fixed date. Our process is short: we hear about the property, review it, and price it on condition.

  1. Send the address and a few lines on your situation.
  2. We review the house and name a price.
  3. You agree, and an escrow or title company schedules closing.
  4. The Utah County Recorder files the deed and you receive payment.

Because we buy as-is, there is no painting, patching or cleaning first. Mention tenants, a lease end date or an unregistered apartment at the start so we can fold them into the offer.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Orem house if it has an unregistered basement apartment?
faqs.a: Yes. An owner has to live in the main home or the apartment, so a conventional buyer may want proof the unit is legal. We buy as it stands, and you need not resolve that beforehand.

faqs.q: How long does Utah County take to record a deed for an Orem sale?
faqs.a: Your title or escrow company normally files it, and your closing agent can tell you the timing.

faqs.q: Does a tenant in my Orem house stop me from selling?
faqs.a: No. Give us the lease terms and any move-out date up front, and the offer will account for them.

faqs.q: Which school district will Orem homes belong to after 2027?
faqs.a: The new Timpanogos district takes over when Alpine School District ends on July 1, 2027. Confirm your address on the boundary map.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an Orem property valuation?
faqs.a: File by September 15. Appeals after that date, up to March 31, are heard only when extra criteria are met and the Board of Equalization accepts them.
